enonce_markdown: A person who can see near objects clearly but cannot see distant objects clearly has which eye defect?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Name the defect from the symptom: short sight is trouble with distant objects, long sight is trouble with near objects.

### Solution

Difficulty in seeing distant objects clearly while near objects are clear is short sight, or myopia. Hypermetropia is long sight, presbyopia is the loss of near vision with age and astigmatism blurs vision because of an uneven cornea.

**Answer: B.**

enonce_markdown: Which type of lens is used in spectacles to correct hypermetropia (long sight)?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

A convex lens converges rays; a concave lens diverges rays. Decide whether the eye needs more or less bending of light.

### Solution

In hypermetropia light is focused behind the retina, so the eye needs extra bending of light. A convex (converging) lens does this and moves the image forward onto the retina. A concave lens corrects short sight.

**Answer: D.**

enonce_markdown: Ebot, a Form 5 student, can read a book comfortably but the writing on the blackboard is blurred. Where is the image of the blackboard formed in his eye, and which lens would correct the problem?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

First find the defect from the symptoms, then recall where light focuses in that defect and which lens moves the image back to the retina.

### Solution

Ebot has myopia (short sight). The eyeball is too long or the lens too strong, so rays from distant objects focus in front of the retina. A concave (diverging) lens spreads the rays slightly before they enter the eye and moves the image back onto the retina.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: In front of the retina; a concave lens
In front of the retina; a convex lens
Behind the retina; a concave lens
Behind the retina; a convex lens

enonce_markdown: An old woman finds that she must hold her newspaper at arm's length to read it, although she saw clearly when she was young. What is the most likely cause?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Near vision needs the lens to become thicker. Ask what could stop the lens from doing this in old age.

### Solution

With age the lens becomes harder and less elastic, so it cannot become thicker to focus near objects: this is presbyopia. An eyeball that is too long causes myopia, which is usually present from youth and affects distant objects. An uneven cornea causes astigmatism.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: The cornea has an uneven surface
The lens has become less elastic and cannot thicken enough
The pupil has become too large

enonce_markdown: Compare myopia and hypermetropia by stating, for each defect: (i) one possible cause, (ii) where the image of the object is formed and (iii) the type of lens used for correction. *(6 marks)*
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Short sight and long sight are opposite defects. Describe the eyeball or lens, the position of the image relative to the retina, and the lens that corrects it.

### Solution

| | Myopia (short sight) | Hypermetropia (long sight) |
|---|---|---|
| Cause | Eyeball too long or lens too strong | Eyeball too short or lens too weak |
| Image formed | In front of the retina (distant objects) | Behind the retina (near objects) |
| Correcting lens | Concave (diverging) lens | Convex (converging) lens |

enonce_markdown: A man's relaxed eye focuses parallel rays from a distant tree at a point in front of his retina. When he looks at a book 25 cm away, he reads it clearly without spectacles. Name his defect and explain why he sees the book clearly but the tree blurred. State how it can be corrected. *(5 marks)*
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Compare the position of the focus for far and near objects, remembering that the lens of the eye can thicken to see near objects.

### Solution

His defect is **myopia (short sight)**. Parallel rays from the distant tree are focused in front of the retina, so the tree appears blurred. Rays from a near object are diverging as they enter the eye. They need more bending than parallel rays, so the focus is farther back and falls on the retina; he can therefore read the book clearly. The defect is corrected by wearing spectacles or contact lenses with a **concave (diverging) lens**, which moves the focus back onto the retina.
